{"arguments": [
 {"id": "G1", "name": "Trinity as single axiom paying four debts", "conclusion": "The Trinitarian God is the single axiom that grounds existence, distinction, relation, and orientation, which every other ontology assumes but cannot derive.", "speaker": "Framework author",
  "premises": [
   "Every formal system has an unprovable floor (set theory nine axioms, Peano five, GR two postulates).",
   "Every system uses four things it cannot ground: existence, distinction, relation, orientation.",
   "The Trinity pays all four from one structure: aseity grounds existence, the persons ground distinction, perichoresis grounds relation, love grounds orientation.",
   "No other ontology derives these four; they are assumed and never paid for."
  ],
  "strength": {
   "st1": {"v": 2, "quote": "That single structure pays four debts no other ontology on earth pays."},
   "st2": {"v": 2, "quote": "Every system that exists -- materialism, idealism, mathematical Platonism, secular humanism -- uses four things it cannot ground: ... Existence ... Distinction ... Relation ... Orientation"},
   "st3": {"v": 1, "quote": "Set theory pays nine axioms. Peano arithmetic pays five. General relativity pays two postulates."},
   "st4": {"v": 1, "quote": "The Trinity pays all four from one structure. Existence is aseity -- the Father IS. Distinction is the persons ... Relation is perichoresis ... Orientation is love"},
   "st5": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st6": {"v": 1, "quote": "No other ontology derives these four; they are assumed, borrowed, and never paid for."},
   "st7": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st8": {"v": 1, "quote": "Every formal system has a floor it cannot dig beneath. Set theory pays nine axioms. Peano arithmetic pays five. General relativity pays two postulates."}
  },
  "prior_art": "Thomas Aquinas, Summa Theologiae (divine simplicity and the Trinitarian processions as ground of being), 1265-1274",
  "originality": {
   "or1": {"v": 1, "quote": "The Trinity pays all four from one structure.", "why": "Aquinas already treats the Trinitarian processions as the ground of all multiplicity and relation; this restates that in axiom/debt vocabulary."},
   "or2": {"v": 1, "quote": "Set theory pays nine axioms. Peano arithmetic pays five. General relativity pays two postulates.", "why": "The formal-system axiom counts are a modern supporting datum the classical prior art does not use."},
   "or3": {"v": 1, "quote": "Everything else derives from this through formal grammar constrained by physics.", "why": "It crosses from formal-systems metatheory and physics into Trinitarian theology."},
   "or4": {"v": 0, "quote": "", "why": "No formalization beyond the debt ledger is given."}
  },
  "weakest_link": "The claim that no other ontology derives existence, distinction, relation and orientation is asserted, not shown for any rival system.",
  "develop_next": "Take one rival ontology (e.g. mathematical Platonism) and show in detail that it must assume all four rather than derive them.",
  "case_map": ["K17", "F1"], "domain": "philosophy"},

 {"id": "G2", "name": "Unprovability as signature of Layer 0", "conclusion": "The inability to prove God is not a weakness but the predicted signature of a genuine root layer.", "speaker": "Framework author",
  "premises": [
   "An axiom that could be proven would rest on something deeper and thus not be the ground.",
   "The derivation grammar predicts a genuine Layer 0 requires nothing beneath it (DG1).",
   "If God could be proven, God would not be the ground.",
   "Godel guarantees this structural limit."
  ],
  "strength": {
   "st1": {"v": 2, "quote": "The inability to prove God is not a weakness but the predicted signature of a genuine root layer."},
   "st2": {"v": 2, "quote": "An axiom that could be proven would rest on something deeper, and then it would not be the ground."},
   "st3": {"v": 1, "quote": "The inability to prove God is exactly what the derivation grammar predicts for a genuine Layer 0: the root layer requires nothing beneath it (DG1)."},
   "st4": {"v": 1, "quote": "If God COULD be proven, God would not be the ground."},
   "st5": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st6": {"v": 1, "quote": "That is not a weakness. It is the signature."},
   "st7": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st8": {"v": 0, "quote": ""}
  },
  "prior_art": "Immanuel Kant, Critique of Pure Reason (the limits of theoretical proof of God), 1781; and Kurt Godel, incompleteness theorems, 1931",
  "originality": {
   "or1": {"v": 1, "quote": "The inability to prove God is exactly what the derivation grammar predicts for a genuine Layer 0", "why": "Kant already argued God cannot be theoretically proven; this reframes the limit as a positive prediction of a bespoke grammar."},
   "or2": {"v": 1, "quote": "the root layer requires nothing beneath it (DG1)", "why": "DG1 is a framework-internal premise absent from the prior art."},
   "or3": {"v": 1, "quote": "God did not make physics because He needed it.", "why": "It links Godel-style metatheory to theology."},
   "or4": {"v": 0, "quote": "", "why": "No formalization of the claim is given."}
  },
  "weakest_link": "The appeal to Godel is loose: Godel's theorems concern formal arithmetic, not the provability of a metaphysical ground.",
  "develop_next": "State precisely which formal system's incompleteness is being invoked and why its unprovability transfers to God.",
  "case_map": ["K17", "F1"], "domain": "philosophy"},

 {"id": "G3", "name": "Physics as created medium for love", "conclusion": "God made physics not from need but because creatures capable of freely receiving and returning love require an ordered, non-divine, consequential, temporal, limited, repairable world.", "speaker": "Framework author",
  "premises": [
   "God is free and creation is a gift, not a necessity.",
   "Beings who can genuinely receive and return love need a world that is not God, stable enough to be known, with real consequence, time, limits, and repair.",
   "Physics is the grammar of that world, not the Author.",
   "Physics provides existence/distinction, relation/lawfulness, consequence/cost, time/sequence, and embodiment/public meaning."
  ],
  "strength": {
   "st1": {"v": 2, "quote": "Physics is the ordered created medium where relation, consequence, choice, time, repair, embodiment, and love can become publicly meaningful."},
   "st2": {"v": 2, "quote": "A world that is not God. ... A world stable enough to be known. ... A world with real consequence. ... A world with time. ... A world with limits. ... A world with repair."},
   "st3": {"v": 1, "quote": "If gravity changed its mind, orbits would not exist. If electromagnetism were arbitrary, chemistry would not hold. If entropy had no direction, consequences would dissolve."},
   "st4": {"v": 1, "quote": "Physics is the grammar of that world. It is not the Author."},
   "st5": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st6": {"v": 1, "quote": "God did not make physics because He needed it. He made physics because we needed a world where love could be real"},
   "st7": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st8": {"v": 1, "quote": "Physics begins with the fact that there IS something ... Physical laws are not chains that bind God. They are the conditions under which creatures can relate reliably."}
  },
  "prior_art": "Richard Swinburne, Providence and the Problem of Evil, 1998 (a world with real goods requires regular natural law and genuine choice)",
  "originality": {
   "or1": {"v": 1, "quote": "Physics is the grammar of that world. It is not the Author.", "why": "Swinburne already argues a lawful, consequential world is a necessary condition for significant free choice; this is a variant with the 'grammar' framing."},
   "or2": {"v": 1, "quote": "If gravity changed its mind, orbits would not exist. If electromagnetism were arbitrary, chemistry would not hold.", "why": "It uses specific force properties as supporting data."},
   "or3": {"v": 1, "quote": "Physics provides existence/distinction, relation/lawfulness, consequence/cost, time/sequence, and embodiment/public meaning.", "why": "It maps physics categories onto theological requirements."},
   "or4": {"v": 0, "quote": "", "why": "No model or equation is offered."}
  },
  "weakest_link": "The claim that the six listed conditions are strictly necessary for free love is asserted rather than argued.",
  "develop_next": "Argue for each condition: show that dropping it (e.g. a world with no consequence) makes free love impossible, not merely harder.",
  "case_map": ["K05", "K07", "F2"], "domain": "theology"},

 {"id": "G4", "name": "Physics is not grace", "conclusion": "Physics describes the condition grace answers but is not itself grace.", "speaker": "Framework author",
  "premises": [
   "Grace is God's unmerited favor entering creation from beyond the closed system.",
   "Physics says closed systems run down and open systems can receive from outside.",
   "Gravity is gravity and grace is grace; they are distinct.",
   "A world with gravity is the kind of world where grace can be received as rescue rather than ignored as optional."
  ],
  "strength": {
   "st1": {"v": 2, "quote": "Physics describes the condition grace answers. Physics is not grace."},
   "st2": {"v": 2, "quote": "Theology says grace is God's unmerited favor, entering creation from beyond the closed system. Physics says closed systems run down; open systems can receive energy, information, and order from outside."},
   "st3": {"v": 1, "quote": "Physics says closed systems run down; open systems can receive energy, information, and order from outside."},
   "st4": {"v": 2, "quote": "Gravity is gravity. Grace is grace."},
   "st5": {"v": 2, "quote": "The objection \"Are you saying gravity is grace?\" gets a clean answer: No."},
   "st6": {"v": 2, "quote": "But a world with gravity is the kind of world where grace can be received as rescue rather than ignored as optional."},
   "st7": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st8": {"v": 0, "quote": ""}
  },
  "prior_art": "none known",
  "originality": {
   "or1": {"v": 2, "quote": "Physics describes the condition grace answers. Physics is not grace.", "why": "Distinguishing the created medium from grace itself is a clarifying move, not a standard apologetic argument."},
   "or2": {"v": 1, "quote": "Physics says closed systems run down; open systems can receive energy, information, and order from outside.", "why": "It uses open/closed system thermodynamics as a supporting datum."},
   "or3": {"v": 1, "quote": "a world with gravity is the kind of world where grace can be received as rescue rather than ignored as optional", "why": "It links thermodynamics to soteriology."},
   "or4": {"v": 0, "quote": "", "why": "No formal apparatus."}
  },
  "weakest_link": "The analogy between open thermodynamic systems receiving energy and a creature receiving grace is left unargued.",
  "develop_next": "Specify the disanalogy limits: what exactly transfers from open-system thermodynamics to grace, and what does not.",
  "case_map": ["K05", "F2"], "domain": "theology"},

 {"id": "G5", "name": "Ten forces compose a portrait of one Person", "conclusion": "The measured properties of ten physical structures, read together, compose a portrait so specific that only one Person in history matches it.", "speaker": "Framework author",
  "premises": [
   "Physics tells what each force does, not why.",
   "Gravity's properties (weakest, universal, unshieldable, always attractive, infinite range, patient, curves paths) match grace.",
   "The strong force's properties (strongest, confinement, slack at short range, holds nuclei) match love, and the Hessian matrix independently scored it as the most connected node.",
   "Electromagnetism's properties (self-sustaining light, no degradation, maximum speed, Maxwell's four equations) match truth.",
   "Thermodynamics, information, and other laws similarly map to necessity, the Word, and other divine attributes."
  ],
  "strength": {
   "st1": {"v": 2, "quote": "when you collect the properties of all ten forces and read them together, they compose a portrait so specific that only one Person in history matches it."},
   "st2": {"v": 2, "quote": "Physics measures these properties: weakest of all four fundamental forces (10^36 weaker than EM). Shapes all large-scale structure ... Cannot be shielded ... Always attractive ... Infinite range ... Acts by curving the path ... Patient"},
   "st3": {"v": 1, "quote": "The Hessian matrix -- blind to theology, just computing coupling strengths between ten differential equations -- scored this variable as the most connected node in the entire system."},
   "st4": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st5": {"v": 1, "quote": "The match between ten physical structures and ten spiritual patterns could be coincidence. A determined skeptic could write the exact opposite essay from the same raw physics."},
   "st6": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st7": {"v": 1, "quote": "kill condition: a force with no matching structure"},
   "st8": {"v": 1, "quote": "The Hessian matrix -- blind to theology, just computing coupling strengths between ten differential equations -- scored this variable as the most connected node in the entire system."}
  },
  "prior_art": "none known",
  "originality": {
   "or1": {"v": 2, "quote": "when you collect the properties of all ten forces and read them together, they compose a portrait so specific that only one Person in history matches it.", "why": "Reading measured force properties as a composite portrait of Christ is not a standard prior argument."},
   "or2": {"v": 2, "quote": "The Hessian matrix -- blind to theology, just computing coupling strengths between ten differential equations -- scored this variable as the most connected node in the entire system.", "why": "The Hessian coupling result is evidence the prior art does not use."},
   "or3": {"v": 2, "quote": "Physics calls it the strong nuclear force. ... \"The greatest of these is love.\" -- 1 Corinthians 13:13. The math said it without being asked.", "why": "It connects nuclear physics and linear algebra to Christology."},
   "or4": {"v": 1, "quote": "The Hessian matrix -- blind to theology, just computing coupling strengths between ten differential equations", "why": "A matrix structure is invoked, though not displayed."}
  },
  "weakest_link": "The inference from property resemblance to 'only one Person matches' is an analogy, not a derivation; no matching criterion is specified.",
  "develop_next": "State an independent, pre-registered matching criterion and show that rival candidates fail it, not just that Christ fits.",
  "case_map": ["K06", "K10", "F3"], "domain": "physics"},

 {"id": "G6", "name": "You Are God narrative sequence", "conclusion": "The nine-step sequence from God's self-sufficient goodness to cross and resurrection holds when first principles are stated in the right order.", "speaker": "Framework author",

  ],

   "st3": {"v": 1, "quote": "A closed system decays. Restoration must come from outside without destroying freedom."},
   "st4": {"v": 1, "quote": "Incarnation enters the system without coercing it. Cross and resurrection restore from within while preserving identity."},
   "st5": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st6": {"v": 1, "quote": "The sequence holds when the first principles are stated in the right order"},
   "st7": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st8": {"v": 0, "quote": ""}
  },
  "prior_art": "none known",
  "originality": {
   "or1": {"v": 1, "quote": "Restoration must come from outside without destroying freedom.", "why": "A variant of the standard creation-fall-redemption narrative, recast as a nine-step inference."},
   "or2": {"v": 1, "quote": "A closed system decays.", "why": "It imports thermodynamic decay as a premise."},
   "or3": {"v": 1, "quote": "A closed system decays. Restoration must come from outside without destroying freedom.", "why": "It bridges thermodynamics and soteriology."},
   "or4": {"v": 0, "quote": "", "why": "No formalization."}
  },
  "weakest_link": "Step 5 ('refusal closes the receiver against the source') is asserted; the closure mechanism is not argued.",
  "develop_next": "Show why refusal necessarily closes the receiver, rather than merely damaging the relationship.",
  "case_map": ["K16", "F4"], "domain": "theology"},

 {"id": "G7", "name": "Free witness and the tree", "conclusion": "A free witness is required because appreciation that cannot refuse is not appreciation, and the tree is free will made visible.", "speaker": "Framework author",
  "premises": [
   "A mirror does not count; appreciation that cannot refuse is an echo.",
   "Love creates because abundance overflows into real others who can answer freely.",
   "Freedom without a real choice is just a word, like being free to leave a room with no door.",
   "The adversary merely asks 'Did God really say...?' and independence starts sounding like an upgrade."
  ],
  "strength": {
   "st1": {"v": 2, "quote": "A free witness is required because appreciation that cannot refuse is not appreciation, and the tree is free will made visible."},
   "st2": {"v": 2, "quote": "A mirror does not count. Appreciation that cannot refuse is not appreciation. It is an echo."},
   "st3": {"v": 1, "quote": "Freedom without a real choice is just a word -- like saying someone is free to leave a room that has no door."},
   "st4": {"v": 1, "quote": "The tree in the garden is not a trap. It is free will made visible."},
   "st5": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st6": {"v": 1, "quote": "Love creates because abundance overflows into real others who can answer freely."},
   "st7": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st8": {"v": 0, "quote": ""}
  },
  "prior_art": "Alvin Plantinga, God, Freedom, and Evil, 1974 (free will as necessary for love and the possibility of evil)",
  "originality": {
   "or1": {"v": 1, "quote": "Appreciation that cannot refuse is not appreciation. It is an echo.", "why": "Plantinga already grounds the possibility of evil in the value of free love; this is a rhetorical variant."},
   "or2": {"v": 1, "quote": "The tree in the garden is not a trap. It is free will made visible.", "why": "It adds the tree as a concrete visible instantiation."},
   "or3": {"v": 0, "quote": "", "why": "No cross-domain bridge is made."},
   "or4": {"v": 0, "quote": "", "why": "No formalization."}
  },
  "weakest_link": "The claim that a genuine choice must be physically instantiated by a specific object (the tree) is asserted, not argued.",
  "develop_next": "Argue why free will requires a publicly visible token rather than an internal capacity to refuse.",
  "case_map": ["K08", "F2"], "domain": "theology"},

 {"id": "G8", "name": "Proximity does not guarantee loyalty", "conclusion": "God need not be made impossible to miss because seeing is not choosing and real love requires faith.", "speaker": "Framework author",

   "st2": {"v": 2, "quote": "The adversary was IN heaven. He could see God directly, and he still rebelled. Proximity never guaranteed loyalty."},
   "st3": {"v": 1, "quote": "The adversary was IN heaven. He could see God directly, and he still rebelled."},
   "st4": {"v": 1, "quote": "Seeing is not the same as choosing."},
   "st5": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},

   "st7": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st8": {"v": 0, "quote": ""}
  },
  "prior_art": "John Hick, Evil and the God of Love, 1966 (epistemic distance as necessary for genuine faith)",
  "originality": {
   "or1": {"v": 1, "quote": "Real love needs something sight cannot provide: faith.", "why": "Hick already argued epistemic distance is required for free faith; this is a variant resting on the adversary's rebellion."},
   "or2": {"v": 1, "quote": "The adversary was IN heaven. He could see God directly, and he still rebelled.", "why": "It uses the fall of the adversary as the supporting datum."},
   "or3": {"v": 0, "quote": "", "why": "No cross-domain bridge."},
   "or4": {"v": 0, "quote": "", "why": "No formalization."}
  },
  "weakest_link": "The single case of the adversary's rebellion is too thin to establish that proximity never guarantees loyalty.",
  "develop_next": "Argue the general principle (why direct sight cannot compel love) rather than resting on one narrative case.",
  "case_map": ["K08", "F2"], "domain": "theology"},

 {"id": "G9", "name": "Cross and empty tomb as physics claims", "conclusion": "The cross is successful deployment of the uncorrupted pattern into the broken system, and the empty tomb proves information survives its container and entropy is locally reversed from outside.", "speaker": "Framework author",
  "premises": [
   "On the cross the perfect pattern voluntarily releases itself into the broken system; 'It is finished' is not defeat.",
   "The temple veil tears top to bottom, opened by God not human hands.",
   "The adversary orchestrated the killing blow and triggered the mechanism that ends him.",
   "The empty tomb shows information survives destruction of its container and entropy is locally reversed by connecting to an external source."
  ],
  "strength": {
   "st1": {"v": 2, "quote": "The empty tomb proves information survives its container and entropy is locally reversed from outside."},
   "st2": {"v": 2, "quote": "First: information survives the destruction of its container. The pattern is not erased when the substrate is. Second: entropy ... gets locally reversed by connecting the system to a source outside itself."},
   "st3": {"v": 1, "quote": "The temple veil tears top to bottom -- not opened from below by human hands, opened from the top, by God."},
   "st4": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st5": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st6": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st7": {"v": 0, "quote": ""},
   "st8": {"v": 0, "quote": ""}
  },
  "prior_art": "none known",
  "originality": {
   "or1": {"v": 2, "quote": "The empty tomb proves information survives its container and entropy is locally reversed from outside.", "why": "Recasting resurrection as information preservation and local entropy reversal is not a standard prior argument."},
   "or2": {"v": 1, "quote": "Second: entropy -- the rule that everything falls apart when left alone -- gets locally reversed by connecting the system to a source outside itself.", "why": "It uses thermodynamics and information theory as supporting data."},
   "or3": {"v": 2, "quote": "information survives the destruction of its container", "why": "It bridges information theory to resurrection."},
   "or4": {"v": 0, "quote": "", "why": "No formalization."}
  },
  "weakest_link": "The premise that resurrection is literally information surviving its container is an analogy, not an established physical result.",
  "develop_next": "Specify what physical quantity is being conserved and what measurement would distinguish survival of information from its loss.",
  "case_map": ["K16", "F4"], "domain": "theology"},

   "or2": {"v": 1, "quote": "A determined skeptic could write the exact opposite essay from the same raw physics.", "why": "It adds an adversarial test the prior art does not use."},
   "or3": {"v": 0, "quote": "", "why": "No cross-domain bridge."},

   "or2": {"v": 1, "quote": "| Gravity | Grace | Agency -- grace can be refused |", "why": "The ten-row table is new evidence."},
